rationale: MIRRI digitalisation/recovery-plan hub: durable publisher of SK digital programme lines whose procurement exposes integrators serving banks.
EU-funds beneficiary register is valuable structured signal but URL check failed and legal terms unclear — recheck liveness and ITMS21+ successor.
Calls portal gives earliest signal of upcoming SK digitalisation/financial-infrastructure spend ahead of vendor-naming tenders.
National open-data catalogue offers machine-readable EU-funds/procurement exports, a stable ingestion path over fragile front-ends.
Commission cohesion data platform: structured SK allocation/spend datasets for sizing digitalisation envelopes; EN and comparable.
Cleaned TED+UVO contracting data would give supplier-level market shares, but URL verification failed and reuse terms unclear — recheck.
IFI award notices name suppliers, but ECEPP typically requires registration — a human must clear access first.
EBRD SK country feed names client financial institutions and digitalisation project scope; public and durable.
Corporate-procurement sub-page of ebrd.com with weak SK banking-vendor yield; covered by monitoring the EBRD parent.
EIB project register names SK financial intermediaries on intermediated credit lines — direct bank/partnership mapping.
EIF discloses each guarantee with the named SK intermediary bank — strong competitor and product-roadmap signal.
Third-party association profile page of SIH, a one-off descriptive artifact; the SIH/SZRB primary site would be the real source.
Static legacy EFSI scoreboard for SK; useful cross-check once, not a continuing signal producer.
MFSR pointer sub-page to EIB/EBRD relations; adds little beyond the IFI registers already tracked.
SEDIA portal exposes SK financial-sector participants in EU programmes but deeper functions need an EU Login account.
Governance explainer page on the partnership-agreement site; contextual only, parent programme monitoring suffices.
SK trade journalism naming bidders and tender controversies is useful vendor-reputation context, but URL check failed and access unclear.
OCP registry entry describes SK/TED dataset coverage and endpoints — mine once to pick a stable ingestion path.
Statutory PSD2 register is the definitive SK payments competitor universe and the anchor for A6 mapping.
Daily-refreshed JSON API of PSD2 institutions — directly ingestible structured backbone of the payments register.
Master NBS supervised-entity database with bulk export: broadest single actor list for SK banking plus payments.
PI/AISP supervision section covers licensing and EEA passporting notifications, signalling foreign PSPs entering SK.
Licensing condition mandating disclosure of outsourcing and external ICT providers — highest-value regulator-side vendor lead.
DORA hub covering the register of ICT third-party arrangements: the most systematic vendor-to-institution mapping available.
Final NBS decisions reveal licences, sanctions, ownership changes and market entries/exits among SK banking and payment actors.
Official NBS gazette carries authoritative decisions and measures shaping SK payment-market structure and reporting duties.
Names the payment systems and schemes under NBS oversight, identifying infrastructure operators and their technology suppliers.
Oversight framework page (PFMI, SIPS, PISA, CROE) defines compliance criteria driving vendor and resilience demand in SK payments.
